about.title: Merced Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Merced County looks different from one street to the next. Some people spend their days in warehouses and shops near W 16th Street; others drive routes along G Street, R Street, and M Street for deliveries, service calls, or field work. When something goes wrong on the clock, California's workers' compensation system is normally the only claim you can bring against your employer, and it pays regardless of who was at fault. That is the part most Merced workers already know. What often gets missed is the second question: did a subcontractor, a property owner, an equipment manufacturer, or another driver play a role? If so, a separate injury claim may be available, and it runs on a two-year deadline rather than the workers' comp timeline. Merced recorded 246 injury collisions in 2025, with reports clustering on Friday afternoons, so a fair number of work-related crashes fall into this third-party category. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match you with an independent attorney who handles both sides of the picture on contingency.

items.title: Third-Party Claims Get a Real Look
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or driver is a different story. The attorney you are connected with will check for that second avenue instead of assuming comp is the end of it.

items.title: Deadlines Explained Plainly
items.desc: You have 30 days to report an injury to your employer, and any third-party claim carries California's two-year limit. An independent attorney can lay those dates out so nothing slips while you focus on healing.

items.title: Protection If Your Employer Pushes Back
items.desc: Retaliation for reporting a work injury is illegal in California. If hours get cut or your job is threatened after you file, the attorney can address that alongside the injury claim itself.

items.question: I was hit by another driver while making deliveries on G Street in Merced. Is workers' comp my only option?
items.answer: Probably not. Because you were on the job, workers' comp should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who caused the crash. Since another driver was involved, you may also have a separate injury claim against that driver, which can cover losses comp does not. That third-party claim has a two-year deadline, so it helps to have it evaluated early.

items.question: I did not tell my supervisor right away. Have I lost my rights?
items.answer: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, so the sooner you do it, the better. A late report does not automatically end a claim, but it can create disputes about how and when you were hurt. An attorney can help you document the injury and get the report on file properly.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge me anything, and are you a law firm?
items.answer: No charge, and no, we are not a law firm. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Merced with an independent personal injury attorney. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.
